title: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP: show the full path of the target domain in Activity explorer
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, licensing and Activity explorer background are supported, and searches confirmed the narrowly stated documentation gaps. Two minor corrections remain: the access-review checklist has no corresponding control row, and the action rating should describe preparation for a display change rather than review of an optional capability.

claims.claim: The checklist tells readers to review and remove Activity explorer role access, but the controls table contains no access-control row.
claims.quote: Review who holds the Information Protection roles and the Microsoft 365 roles that Learn lists for Activity explorer, and remove access nobody needs. / The only control row governs how much of the target address Activity explorer shows.
claims.fix: Remove the first Before rollout checklist bullet about reviewing and removing role access; retain the documented role information in Scope and Governance controls. Do not add an unverified control row.

claims.claim: The review action rating treats this display change as an optional capability or a new control.
claims.quote: action: "review" / Endpoint DLP events in Activity explorer are to show the full path of the target domain, not just the domain name. / Tell compliance and security analysts that Endpoint DLP events may show a longer target value than before.
claims.fix: Change action from "review" to "prepare": the standard places a redesign of existing behaviour that needs low-risk communication in prepare, including when its default state is unknown.
